name: Muslim Public Affairs Council Foundation
mission: MPAC improves public understanding and policies that impact American Muslims by engaging our government, media, and communities.
programs: Center for Security, Technology, and Policy (CSTP)
theoryOfChange: The Muslim Public Affairs Council (MPAC) has a "2026–2030 Strategic Plan" which serves as a roadmap for their work, outlining strategic focus areas to advance justice, dignity, and constitutional rights for American Muslim communities. [14] Additionally, MPAC utilizes a "Human Security Now" policy framework, which is described as their flagship policy framework. This framework centers the impact of policy decisions on everyday people and encourages policymakers to prioritize four freedoms: Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want, Freedom of Expression, and Freedom of Worship, enabling a comprehensive analysis of potential policy decisions. [2, 4, 6]

rich_narrative.summary:
The Muslim Public Affairs Council Foundation works to improve public policy and media representation for American Muslims. <cite id="3">In FY2024, the organization reported Total Revenue of $4,252,481</cite> to support its civil rights, policy advocacy, and community education initiatives. Operating since 1988, the organization maintains key programs such as Government Affairs & Advocacy, the Center for Security, Technology, and Policy, and Media & Hollywood Engagement. The group produces detailed educational resources, including <cite id="6">security bulletins</cite>, policy reports on <cite id="7">international relations and civil liberties</cite>, and community toolkits like <cite id="9">guides for religious leaders</cite> and <cite id="8">K-12 educational plans</cite>.

Financial data from FY2024 shows that the organization operated with a <cite id="3">57.1% program expense ratio</cite>, which trails the advocacy sector peer median of 79.4%. However, fundraising costs remain efficient at <cite id="1">$0.18 per $1 raised</cite>, and the foundation maintains strong short-term stability with <cite id="1">21.4 months of working capital reserves</cite>. The organization accepts zakat, allowing donors to support systemic policy and media advocacy through <cite id="2">zakat-eligible contributions</cite>.
